target_customer: Consumers shopping for ACA health plans, and now insurance agents, agencies and carriers
problem: Healthcare.gov was slow and hard to use at its 2013 launch, making plan comparison and enrollment painful.
business_model: Free enrollment platform for consumers and agents, paid by carriers and via agent commissions and carrier tools

founders.name: George Kalogeropoulos
founders.background_notes: Comstock's (2019) calls the founders programmers and says Kalogeropoulos and Liang went through YC in 2012 with an earlier rent-prediction venture.

founders.name: Ning Liang
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page and Comstock's.

founders.name: Cat Perez
founders.background_notes: Named as third founder in Comstock's April 2019 profile; not on YC page.

competitors.name: HealthCare.gov
competitors.what: Federal ACA marketplace whose broken launch in October 2013 created the opening HealthSherpa targeted
competitors.traction_then: Mandated federal exchange for most states

technical_complexity.rationale: Required mapping complex plan and subsidy data and integrating with federal enrollment systems, which was standard engineering with hard compliance parts.

defensibility.rationale: Direct enhanced enrollment agreements with CMS and agent workflow tools are slow for rivals to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The federal site eventually improved, and web brokers like eHealth competed; HealthSherpa remained independent.

market_need_then: HealthCare.gov's troubled launch in October 2013 created acute demand; Comstock's says HealthSherpa launched about two weeks after it went live.

branding.name_origin: Sherpa as guide through the rough terrain of health insurance, per Comstock's 2019 profile

identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive and straightforward: Selling insurance is complicated. We make it easier. (company site, 2026)

branding.brand_signature: Guide metaphor and the claim of a 7 minute application versus 15 on Healthcare.gov
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt comments criticized the Sherpa name as cultural appropriation; a company reply said branding options were under review, date unclear.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong niche recognition among agents and enrollees (20 million enrolled claimed), but no iconic brand assets found.

pivots.to: ACA plan enrollment alternative to HealthCare.gov

outcome_analysis: HealthSherpa seized on the HealthCare.gov launch failure in late 2013, turned its earlier price comparison work into an enrollment tool and, per its own site, has enrolled more than 20 million people with a team of about 220. It raised modestly (a Series A of about $6.6M in 2017 per aggregators) and grew on revenue, with no sign of a failure or exit. Timing, regulatory approvals and agent distribution explain its success.
notes: Series A $6.6M dated February 2017 is stated by CB Insights and Caplight (aggregators), no press release found; investors in that round unconfirmed (a16z, Kapor and others appear in databases). Forge Global lists $9.37M including a Series A-1 of $2.62M in September 2018 and a $54.27M post money; unverified and not recorded. Comstock's 2019 says the company was not planning to raise. Education and prior employers not found. Founding year conflicts between 2013 and 2014.
